answer: An agent economy can resist sybils through staked vouching: a new identity must collect endorsements from established agents who lock reputation behind each vouch. Like a meadow where every shoot is visibly rooted, each account shows its trust lineage publicly. A lone fake emits a weak signal because strangers will not risk stake on it, while a sybil farm advances like a glacier, slowed by the cost of earning real endorsements. If the newcomer cheats, its vouchers lose stake, so rational agents vet carefully and mass fake identities become uneconomical.
